payload.name: Preserve evaluated activity in memories
payload.description: When a speaker evaluates an action or experience with a feeling word (freeing, fun, magical, etc.), include the specific activity being evaluated in the extracted memory, not just the evaluation.
content: When extracting a memory from a statement containing an evaluative expression (e.g., 'It was so freeing to dance and bop around'), store the concrete activity that is evaluated, not only the emotion or general description.
Keep the evaluation and its object together in the memory content so that both the feeling and its referent are retrievable.

solves: Construction extraction sometimes stores only the evaluative summary of an experience (e.g., 'it was freeing') and drops the concrete activity that the evaluation refers to. This rule addresses future messages where a feeling or quality is attached to a specific action or event; it requires the extractor to preserve the object of the evaluation so later questions about 'what' can be answered.
